To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
RV systolic pressure load leads to RV myocytes that are longer and more binucleated and have less myofibrils.
fetal RVSP load stimulates fetal myocyte maturation, as indicated by increased binucleation, and increases myocyte size.
right ventricular systolic load in fetal sheep increases myocyte size and promotes myocyte binucleate maturation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of right ventricle systolic pressure load on fetal myocytes.
the effects of right ventricle (RV) pressure load on the maturation of fetal RV and left ventricle (LV) myocytes.
understanding the effects of right ventricle (RV) systole pressure (RVSP)-load on fetal cardiac growth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RVSP-load stimulates myocyte enlargement, binucleation, and myofibrilogenesis in the RV but has minor effects on myocytes in the left ventricle.
fetal RV systolic load stimulates myocyte maturation (increases the proportion of binucleated myocytes) and hypertrophy (myocyte enlargement).
RVSP load in the near-term fetus stimulates RV myocyte growth and maturation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RV systolic pressure load leads to RV hypertrophy and myocyte maturation, but not to left ventricular hypertrophy or myocyte maturation.
RVSP load in fetal sheep leads to myocyte enlargement and maturation, and these changes are associated with increased RV mass.
fetal myocyte growth is influenced by both ventricles, and myocyte maturation is influenced primarily by the right ventricle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fetal heart is a dynamic, plastic organ that is able to adapt to changes in loading.
the fetal heart can respond to increased pressure load by hypertrophic and hyperplastic growth.
fetal RV systolic load induces RV myocyte enlargement and maturation, and that these processes are independent of LV systolic load.
